governance.decisionForum: King’s Edge Portfolio Board, with the team’s organisational, workforce and professional-practice arrangements governed through the relevant Digital and IT forums.
governance.decisionScope: Material decisions about the team’s remit; the four funded Year One posts and their grades, start dates and recurrent implications; the shared-capacity deployment model outside those posts; whether solution architecture is covered within the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer post or separately; leadership and decision rights; demand intake and prioritisation; the evidence the first year must generate about team shape and institutional capability; any material increase in first-year Hub scope that would compete with the King’s Edge roadmap; product and delivery practices; interfaces with specialist Digital and IT functions; evidence-based decisions to expand the team; handover criteria; and enduring institutional ownership.
governance.businessAsUsualOwner: TBC – Digital and IT product development capability owner
governance.businessAsUsualOwnershipNote: The capability is expected to sit within Digital and IT. The Year One funded core is 4.0 FTE across four explicit posts: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE UX/UI Designer and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. The current staffing cost envelope is £201,000 for approximately November 2026 to June 2027, pending Digital and IT grading and start-date validation. Alongside those funded posts, the working Year One deployment hypothesis is approximately 2.5 FTE-equivalent of named existing/shared capacity: 0.3 FTE Product Owner, 0.5 FTE delivery coordination/agile facilitation, 0.5 FTE service design, 0.5 FTE business analysis, 0.2 FTE user research, 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, 0.2 FTE pooled technical/assurance input and 0.1 FTE live-service/support collaboration. Add up to 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the senior engineering post cannot carry that function. These shared-capacity assumptions require James Costerton and Digital and IT validation and are not additional funded posts at this stage. The enduring organisational home, recurrent staffing, professional leadership and relationship to the Digital Student Experience Hub product and platform ownership under 4.1.2 should be confirmed as the operating model is proven. King’s Edge remains the principal substantive product demand and the September 2027 Hub is a focused first live release.
